minor.issue: Backend correctly returns 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600' (verified via localhost:8001), but the preview ingress (cloudflare) rewrites it to 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate' on the public URL. This means clients/CDNs on the public domain will not cache the legal pages. App code is correct; this is an infra/proxy configuration concern only — likely intentional for the preview env but worth verifying for the prod ingress before Play Store submission since Google may re-fetch the pages frequently.

action_items: (Optional infra) Verify that the production ingress preserves 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600' on /api/legal/* responses — currently the preview cloudflare layer strips it. Backend code is fine; just an ingress rule to confirm before Play Store submission.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/routers/legal.py uses lru_cache on _load(slug) but the cached html bakes in datetime.now() into the body as a 'Effective' marker via md.replace('[DATE]', today). Because the cache key is just slug, the effective-date string is frozen at first-load forever (until process restart). For a 1-hour Cache-Control window this is fine, but if the app runs for days, the displayed date will drift. Recommend either: (a) remove lru_cache and compute fresh on each request (HTML render is ~ms cheap), or (b) move the date stamping into the response layer (legal_html function) so only the markdown→HTML conversion is cached.

/app/backend/routers/legal.py: legal_text reads the file fresh on every call (no lru_cache), but legal_html caches the rendered output indefinitely. Inconsistent caching strategy. Recommend matching behavior.

/app/backend/routers/legal.py _md_to_html is a custom mini-markdown parser. It works for the maintained docs, but if a future contributor adds tables, blockquotes, fenced code blocks, or numbered lists, they will render incorrectly. Consider a one-line dependency (markdown or markdown-it-py from pip) to future-proof — or document in the file header the supported subset.

Activity-log volume concern: every checklist item add/edit/remove writes one db.activity doc. On a busy company toggling many items per job, this could grow db.activity quickly. There's already an index on (company_id, created_at) so query perf is fine, but consider TTL or archival policy for activity rows older than ~90 days.

JobChecklistPanel.jsx: loadTemplates() is now async but is invoked unawaited inside useEffect (line 41). Works fine because the function handles its own setState, but a follow-up that wants to chain logic after templates load (e.g., auto-open the select if there's only one template) won't be able to await it. Minor — current behavior is correct.

rca of the issue: No application bugs found. One env-level finding only: the cloudflare layer in front of the preview URL rewrites the backend-set 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600' header to 'no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate'. Reproduction: curl -sI http://localhost:8001/api/legal/privacy → shows 'cache-control: public, max-age=3600'; curl -sI https://a1-dispatch.preview.emergentagent.com/api/legal/privacy → shows 'cache-control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate'. Mitigation: verify prod ingress (NOT preview cloudflare) does not apply the same override before Play Store submission; if it does, configure the prod ingress to honor upstream Cache-Control on /api/legal/* paths.
